rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation changes predictions clamp minimum from 1e-12 to 1e-11. With shape [128, 4096], when predictions contains mostly zeros with one small positive value (e.g., 1e-7), the clamp sum differs: original sum ≈ 1e-7 + 4095*1e-12 ≈ 1e-7, mutated sum ≈ 1e-7 + 4095*1e-11 ≈ 5.1e-7. After normalization, original p[0] ≈ 0.9999 vs mutated p[0] ≈ 0.196. With targets concentrated at position 0, KL divergence differs by ~1.6 (using log(1/0.196) - log(1/0.9999)).
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the clamp minimum for predictions from 1e-12 to 1e-11. When predictions have many near-zero or zero values, this creates a significant difference in the sum used for normalization. With seq_len=4096, the sum of clamped zeros differs by factor of 10 (4096*1e-12 vs 4096*1e-11). When one element is small but dominates (e.g., 1e-7), the mutated version has a much larger denominator due to accumulated 1e-11 values, causing the normalized distribution to shift significantly. This propagates through KL divergence calculation as log(p) differences.
rounds.kill_strategy: Create predictions with one small positive value (e.g., 1e-7 at position 0) and zeros elsewhere. Create targets with probability mass concentrated at position 0. The difference in clamp thresholds will cause significant normalization differences, leading to large KL divergence differences exceeding the tolerance.
rounds.recommendations: When using clamp for numerical stability with very small thresholds, test with inputs that are entirely or mostly zeros to verify the clamp threshold choice doesn't significantly affect downstream computations like normalization and divergence calculations.
rounds.suggested_code:
def generate_inputs(device):
    # Create predictions with one small positive value and mostly zeros
    # This maximizes the impact of clamp threshold difference on normalization
    predictions = torch.zeros(128, 4096, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
    predictions[:, 0] = 1e-7  # Small positive value at position 0
    
    # Create targets concentrated at position 0 to maximize KL impact
    targets = torch.zeros(128, 4096, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
    targets[:, 0] = 1.0  # All probability mass at position 0
    
    return [predictions, targets]
